items.title: A ring map inducing a universal homeomorphism on spectra is a filtered colimit of finitely presented algebras inducing universal homeomorphisms, and the same with residue field isomorphisms
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a ring map inducing a universal homeomorphism on spectra is a filtered colimit of finitely presented algebras with the same property, and likewise with isomorphisms on residue fields added (statement lines 11910-11923). The counted proof runs 57 lines and has two genuinely different layers: the criterion for filtered colimits of finitely presented algebras together with the inheritance of universal homeomorphisms by subalgebras gives the reduction to a largeness claim, and the claim itself is proved by passing to reduced rings, replacing the base by the image of the map, quoting the structure of finite type algebras inducing universal homeomorphisms, and lifting finitely many generators and their square, cube or p-th power relations to a member of the colimit so that the p-th power and 2-3 type lemmas apply (proof lines 11926-11980). It is H2 under the lane rule: the proof contains several checkable constructions and reductions, not a restatement, and the only deferral is part (2), which the author declares to have exactly the same proof as the fully proved part (1).
